# Copilot Instructions for "o som do silêncio"

This is a Jekyll-based blog about music and personal experiences. The site is deployed to GitHub Pages at osomdosilencio.com.br.

## Build, Test & Deployment

### Local Development
```bash
# Install dependencies (Ruby 3.2+)
bundle install

# Start local development server
bundle exec jekyll serve

# Build for production
bundle exec jekyll build
```

The development server runs on `http://localhost:4000`. Jekyll rebuilds automatically on file changes.

### Deployment
The site automatically builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on push to `main` branch via `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. The workflow:
1. Checks out the repository (including submodules)
2. Sets up Ruby 3.2 with bundler caching
3. Installs dependencies with platform-specific lockfile updates
4. Builds with `bundle exec jekyll build`
5. Deploys to `gh-pages` branch with custom domain `osomdosilencio.com.br`

## High-Level Architecture

### Directory Structure
- `_posts/` - Blog posts (markdown files with date prefix: `YYYY-MM-DD-title.md`)
- `_pages/` - Static pages (about, archive, categories, tags)
- `_layouts/` - Liquid templates for post, page, archive rendering
- `_includes/` - Reusable Liquid components (pagination, post cards, sharing, TOC, etc.)
- `_sass/` - SCSS stylesheets
- `assets/` - Images and other static assets
- `.jekyll-cache/` & `_site/` - Build artifacts (excluded from git)

### Site Configuration
Configuration is in `_config.yml`:
- **Markdown engine**: Kramdown with GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM)
- **Syntax highlighting**: Rouge with line numbers enabled
- **Plugins**: jekyll-paginate-v2, jekyll-sitemap, jekyll-feed, jekyll-seo-tag, jekyll-archives
- **Language/locale**: Portuguese (pt_BR)
- **Author info**: Defined in config, keyed by username (e.g., `igor`)

### Post/Page Metadata
All posts and pages use YAML front matter. Required fields:
```yaml
---
layout: post  # or 'page'
title: "Title"
description: "Short description for SEO"
date: YYYY-MM-DD
author: igor  # must match key in _config.yml authors section
categories: [category-name]  # lowercase, kebab-case
featured: false  # true for featured posts on homepage
image: /assets/images/filename.jpeg
---
```

Categories are hierarchical and generate archive pages via jekyll-archives plugin.

## Key Conventions

### Naming Conventions
- **Post files**: `YYYY-MM-DD-title-in-kebab-case.md` (date prefix required)
- **Categories**: lowercase, kebab-case (e.g., `post-hardcore`, `alternative-rock`)
- **Images**: kebab-case with descriptive names under `/assets/images/`

### Content Standards
- Posts are written in Portuguese or English (mixed allowed)
- Descriptions should be concise, suitable for SEO and social sharing
- Featured images are required (JPEG preferred for compatibility)
- Category names should match music genres or content themes already in use

### Liquid Templating
- Post layout automatically renders post content with author, date, categories
- Archive pages generated by jekyll-archives for categories and tags
- Pagination via jekyll-paginate-v2 (configured per layout)
- TOC (table of contents) available via `{% include toc.html %}` include

### Content Organization
- Categories organize posts (generated archive pages: `/category/:name/`)
- Posts typically analyze or discuss a song, album, or musical concept
- Use descriptive titles reflecting the subject matter (song/artist name common)
- Leverage pagination for category and tag archive pages

### Plugin-Specific Notes
- **jekyll-seo-tag**: Automatically generates SEO tags; title and description from front matter
- **jekyll-feed**: RSS feed generated at `/feed.xml`
- **jekyll-sitemap**: Sitemap generated at `/sitemap.xml`
- **kramdown options**: GFM syntax enabled, Rouge line numbers enabled by default

### Deployment Considerations
- Build outputs excluded from version control (`.jekyll-cache`, `_site`)
- Custom domain configured in GitHub Pages settings and deploy workflow
- Keep `Gemfile.lock` updated; workflow auto-patches for Linux runner compatibility
- Workflow requires no secrets beyond default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
